# Results — Study 126 (Parabolic-SAR) on real daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). One recipe — Wilder's
Parabolic SAR (AF init 0.02, step 0.02, cap 0.20) on daily bars: go *long* on an
upward flip (SAR crosses below price), *short* on a downward flip, enter at the next
bar's open, exit on a symmetric take-profit/stop of **±1 ATR(20)**, capped at 60 bars.
Run across a basket of six liquid ETFs (SPY, QQQ, IWM, GLD, TLT, EEM) — ten years of
daily bars — and pinned against a **random-direction control** on the same flip dates.
As-of **2026-06-14**.*

## The honest test — symmetric ±1 ATR(20), gross (cost = 0)

A direction-symmetric payoff is the only fair way to ask *"does the SAR flip point the
right way?"* — with TP and SL equidistant, a coin earns ≈ 0.

| Arm | n trades | win-rate | mean (bps/trade) | skew | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Parabolic SAR (with the flip)** | 1,335 | **53.3%** | **+9.34** | −0.07 | **+2.47** |
| Random direction (control) | 1,335 | 50.9% | +2.18 | — | +0.50 |

- **Pooled**: gross HAC *t* = **+2.47**, just above the inference bar of 2.
- **Per-instrument, no single ticker clears |t| ≥ 2.0**: SPY +1.05, QQQ +0.67, IWM +0.80,
  GLD +0.19, TLT +1.53, EEM +1.75.  The pooled significance is diluted across a basket
  of uncorrelated tickers, not driven by a single dominant ticker.
- **Δ vs coin**: SAR − random = **+7.15 bps/trade** — the flip direction does add something
  over a coin, but the control also has a positive (noise) mean (+2.18 bps), so the signal
  over baseline is modest.

**Verdict:** The pooled t barely clears 2, but the per-ticker breakdown does not
support a confident REAL stamp. The result is **WEAK** — a small, fragile directional
tilt that pooling amplifies to nominal significance.

## Could you trade it? — the cost sweep

At ~**22.6 flips/ticker/year** (round-trips, not one-way), even modest costs are lethal:

| round-trip cost | net mean (bps/trade) | HAC *t* | annualised gross equivalent |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 0.0 bps (gross) | +9.34 | +2.47 | ~+2.1%/yr |
| 1.0 bps | +8.34 | +2.21 | ~+1.9%/yr |
| 2.0 bps | +7.34 | +1.94 | ~+1.7%/yr |
| 5.0 bps | +4.34 | +1.15 | ~+1.0%/yr |
| 10.0 bps  | −0.66 | −0.18 | ~−0.2%/yr |

At 2 bps per round-trip (realistic for an ETF via a no-commission broker with bid-ask
spread), the HAC *t* drops to +1.94 — below the significance bar.  At 5 bps (more
realistic once slippage is included) the annualised return falls to ~1% and the *t*
collapses to +1.15.  **There is no realistic execution scenario that yields a confident,
investable edge.**

No individual ticker clears |*t*| ≥ 2.  EEM shows the largest point estimate (+20 bps,
*t* = +1.75) — the most trend-persistent instrument in the basket (emerging markets
tend to trend more than US large-caps) — but still below significance on its own.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery works when there's something to find

On a deterministic synthetic daily tape (`data.synthetic_daily`), the same engine
recovers a SAR edge **only when bar-level momentum is planted**, and reads ≈ 0 when it
isn't — confirming the rule is a faithful momentum harvester:

| Planted bar AR(1) momentum | SAR gross (bps/trade) | beats random control? |
|---|--:|:--:|
| 0.00 (martingale) | ≈ 0 (coin) | no |
| +0.20 (persistence) | positive, *t* > 2 | yes |
| −0.10 (reversion) | negative | no (wrong side) |

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.**  Pooled gross HAC *t* = +2.47 (marginal), but zero individual
  ticker clears |*t*| ≥ 2, and the control arm is itself positive (+2.18 bps),
  suggesting a noise baseline that inflates the margin.  Literature support for Parabolic
  SAR in trending regimes is real but contingent on regime identification, which is
  circular.
- **Tradability — FRAGILE.**  Gross annualised ≈ +2.1%/yr at ~22 round-trips/yr; 2 bps
  per round-trip wipes the statistical significance, and 5 bps wipes most of the return.
  No known venue delivers 0–1 bps all-in on large ETFs consistently.
